customer_updates.name: Kiran M
customer_updates.text: "I recently attended the urban art festival at Sassoon Docks in Mumbai and it was an incredible experience! The venue was transformed into a stunning display of color and creativity with amazing murals and street art from talented artists. The atmosphere was lively and interactive, with live music, food stalls, and opportunities to participate in art workshops. I highly recommend this festival to anyone who loves art and wants to experience it in a unique setting. Don't miss out on this amazing event!"

featured_reviews.name: Aatul Gaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text: A true reflection of Mumbai's fishing heritage. The early morning activity, colorful boats, and hardworking fishing community make Sassoon Dock a memorable and authentic experience. Highly recommended for photography enthusiasts and culture lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Tripho India
featured_reviews.review_text: A Wonderful place to visit in South Bombay and One time experience of visiting one of the largest fishing market in Mumbai. Beautiful street Art fishing boats are the main attraction of the place

featured_reviews.name: Shivam Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best place for the fish lover. From prawns to sword fish you will get varieties of fish here. There are auctions also for fish baskets which happen between 4.00 to 5.30 (only if you want it in a bulk quantity). I visited this place on Sunday at 5.30 but still there are a lot of rush. Remember one this if you want to negotiate, do the cold negotiation by showing your fingers (if you want it for ₹400 then show 4 fingers) that way they will give you without letting the price to others. Sunrise here is also amazing 🤩. Must visit this place.

featured_reviews.name: vikram pawar
featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh fish availabe at this spot.First time I see black heron at this place

featured_reviews.name: Yossi Gabay
featured_reviews.review_text:
The fish market is located at the Sasson Pier. The pier is named after the Jewish merchant and philanthropist David Sasson, who also built a large library, a synagogue, and more. The fish market is  very

busy, it is very difficult to walk on the pier due to the crowding. The fishermen bring their fish to the pier and merchants of all kinds buy and sell the fish. The hustle and bustle is very big. Very colorful and interesting. We arrived before six in the morning.

featured_reviews.name: No Mad
featured_reviews.review_text: A must visit place to understand and see real life of Market and Fisheries

featured_reviews.name: Marcos O. Diogo
featured_reviews.review_text: It is a great place to get lost in Indian fishing culture; we loved the authenticity we found there. A must-visit during your Mumbai stay if you have a chance to get a local guide to walk you around and tell you the history; you'll reward yourself with a much better experience. The whole area gives you a taste of Indian heritage

featured_reviews.name: Paul Draskovich
featured_reviews.review_text: Worth visitng as long as you can stomach the stench of fish that was so strong it stays in your clothes.  Came before sunrise to photograph and for that, it over delivers.  Having witnessed the morning I was not motivated to eat any fish whilst in Mumbai.

I am not disappointed, but I am not impressed, so this may be a one-time visit to the restaurant.
The prawn fry was good, but the surmai and bombil fry were very disappointing because they were so oily and the bombil had not been drained of water.

featured_reviews.name: Buccaneer2.0
featured_reviews.review_text:
Islam Gymkhana - 4 Stars 🌟🌟🌟🌟

A historic gem in Mumbai, Islam Gymkhana has stood proudly on Marine Drive since its establishment in 1890, representing more than just sports—it’s a cultural landmark. The lush green lawns outside are nothing short of stunning, offering a serene escape in the heart of the bustling city. 🌳✨

The view? Simply spectacular! Picture this: the expansive sky merging with the Arabian Sea, a golden sunset painting the horizon, the smooth stretch of Marine Drive, and the comforting feel of the grassy lawns underfoot. 🌅🌴 The perfect combination of natural beauty and urban life.

What makes it even more convenient is the location—just steps away from the railway station exit, making it easily accessible for everyone. 🚉 A stroll here feels like stepping into a calm oasis, where the rush of the city meets the soothing sound of the waves. 🌊

Whether you’re here for a game, an event, or just to soak in the peaceful vibes, Islam Gymkhana offers a slice of serenity in the heart of Mumbai’s hustle. Truly a place where history meets beauty!

featured_reviews.name: Ashraf Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Islam Gymkhana is a historic social & sporting club located on Marine Drive.
The land was allotted in 1890, and the club has a large, sea-facing property (around 19,300 sq. m) with both open grounds and built-up areas.
Membership used to be restricted to Muslims but now is open to people of all communities.

They have massage, steam & jacuzzi facility for members. Restroom facility available for members & guest. They have a car parking facility for guest. featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently attended a wedding at Kora Kendar, and while the overall ambience was pleasant, I was disappointed with the lack of proper washroom facilities. Having previously visited for a garba event a few years ago, I expected improvements in this area, but unfortunately, it was still a major inconvenience.

The venue relies on portable restrooms, commonly known as porta-potties, which are known for their discomfort and lack of cleanliness. This arrangement was highly inconvenient, especially during a wedding where guests require comfortable and hygienic washroom facilities. The absence of proper washroom amenities significantly affected the overall experience.

However, it's worth noting that Kora Kendar does excel in terms of ambiance. The atmosphere created for the event was enjoyable, and the management seemed to have put effort into creating a pleasant environment for the guests. The overall decor and arrangements were satisfactory, contributing to the positive aspects of the venue.

Despite the shortcomings in washroom facilities, Kora Kendar may still be a suitable choice for events like garba or weddings, provided that alternative arrangements are made for washroom facilities. It would greatly enhance the overall experience and ensure the comfort of guests.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: anish tatkare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I went to this hotel with my family for a dinner.
The hotel's name is only Taste of Konkan, but there is no taste of Konkan anywhere. I'm from Konkan. So don't fool people by talking about the taste of Konkan.

featured_reviews.name: PARESH SHAH
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kora Kendra Ground 3 – A Spacious & Beautifully Decorated Wedding Venue

Kora Kendra Ground 3 is one of those places that instantly puts you in a celebratory mood. The space is huge, making it perfect for grand weddings, receptions, and big family functions. What really stands out is how beautifully the venue is decorated — elegant lighting, well-planned layout, and a warm ambience that makes every moment feel special.

There’s plenty of room for seating, dining, and even those big baraat entries! Parking is usually manageable, and the overall organisation feels smooth and guest-friendly.

If you’re looking for a spacious, classy, and well-maintained venue for a memorable event, Kora Kendra Ground 3 definitely delivers. ✨

True example.
